MhwClimatologySpec.description:
The daily-SST baseline period Marine Heatwave detection (Hobday et
al. 2016) computes its per-day-of-year threshold from. A scientific
choice, not a code default (CLAUDE.md invariant #6) -- previously
mhw_detection.py's own CLIM_START/CLIM_END module constants.
MhwClimatologySpec.title: MhwClimatologySpec

ResponseAggregationSpec.description:
How the per-trial source above rolls up into a period-level series.
A distinct representation from the source itself: the count this
produces exists only here, never per trial -- it counts trials
aggregated into a period, not a biological sample size.

count_field.description: Canonical name for the resulting per-period trial count (e.g. 'n_assays'). Deliberately not 'n': that reads as biological sample size, which this is not.
count_field.title: Count Field

ResponseAggregationSpec.title: ResponseAggregationSpec

ResponseColumnMap.description:
Explicit source-column -> canonical-field mapping for the per-trial
response source. Never deduced from column names: in the current source
sheet, the columns named `pos`/`neg` are NOT controls -- they are
`UL-EC50` and `EC50-LL`, the asymmetric confidence-interval half-widths
(see note-dati-sorgente.md). Declaring the mapping explicitly is what
keeps that kind of misreading from happening again, to a human or to
code working from the sheet.
ResponseColumnMap.title: ResponseColumnMap

ResponseSourceSpec.description: The per-trial (single-bioassay) source: one row per determination.

temporal_resolution.description: Declared, not implied. In the current source, most rows record only the month, not a real day -- treating the dates as day-resolution would be a silent overstatement of precision.
temporal_resolution.title: Temporal Resolution

control_columns.description: Per-trial validity-control replicate columns (e.g. negative-control malformation-rate replicates), present only on a subset of trials. These are fields of the observation, not an independent series -- they share the trial's own date.
control_columns.title: Control Columns

ResponseSourceSpec.title: ResponseSourceSpec

ResponseSpec.description:
A response series: what is measured, on what population/individual,
and how the raw per-trial source becomes the aggregated series most
analyses run on. See docs/roadmap/note-dati-sorgente.md for why each
field here is shaped the way it is.

label.description: Human-readable name for output artifacts (results/ CSV/JSON headers, dashboard labels) -- distinct from `id`, which is a slug. Writing a literal like 'EC50' at an output boundary instead of reading it from here is the artifact-identity invariant (CLAUDE.md #4) being violated, not honored.
label.title: Label

nature.description: What kind of quantity this is. Never default to 'biomarker' as a generic label for 'response series' -- most response series, including the current EC50 case, are not biomarkers, and calling one that is scientifically wrong.
nature.title: Nature

adverse_direction.description: Which way the value moves when the organism's condition gets WORSE -- not 'higher/lower is better', since 'better' flips meaning depending on who's asking and this field must not.
adverse_direction.title: Adverse Direction

split_date.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD): the pre/post regime-shift boundary estimated for THIS response series (docs/adr/0001 -- a rank-based estimate, deliberately not reconciled with changepoint.py's own QLR/AR(1) estimate on the same series). Per-response, not a shared constant: a second response series has its own regime shift, possibly at a different date. Validated at common.py's load time against the actual response series' date range, not here (this module never reads data/).
split_date.title: Split Date

ResponseSpec.title: ResponseSpec

SiteSpec.description:
An oceanographic monitoring site -- in practice, a Copernicus Marine
grid cell (a nearest-cell approximation of the real site; see CLAUDE.md's
"Contesto scientifico utile" on when that approximation breaks down).
SiteSpec.title: SiteSpec

VariableSpec.description:
An environmental variable fetched from a provider. Declared for this
step's completeness; not yet consumed by any fetch script -- see module
docstring.
VariableSpec.title: VariableSpec

WindowSpec.description:
A named temporal window of the study. Declared for completeness; not
yet consumed anywhere -- see module docstring and docs/adr/0000.
WindowSpec.title: WindowSpec

description:
Top-level study specification: everything a case declares about
itself. See examples/livorno_paracentrotus/study.yaml for the current
case, described with exactly today's config.py values.

data_dir.description: Where this study's data/ lives, relative to this study.yaml's own location. Resolved to an absolute path by load_study(), which also checks it exists -- callers (common.py) always see an absolute, existing directory.
data_dir.title: Data Dir

title: StudySpec
